A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

mucosal administration of a heterologous vaccine (MVA) expressing Ag 85A strongly enhances BCG-induced Ag 85A T cell immunity, and mucosal administration of the vaccine also elicits Ag 85A immunity in the lungs, the site of infection.

mucosal administration of BCG and subsequent boosting with recombinant modified Vaccinia virus Ankara (MVA) expressing Ag 85A, a major secreted mycobacterial protein, results in a potent and protective T cell immune response in the lungs of mice, which correlates with protection from aerosol challenge with Mycobacterium Tuberculosis.

mucosal delivery of BCG followed by boosting with recombinant MVA expressing M. tuberculosis Ag85A induces potent Ag85A specific T cell responses and provides unprecedented protection against aerosol challenge with virulent M. tuberculosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

mucosal immunization with BCG followed by mucosal boosting with BCG or recombinant modified Vaccinia Ankara expressing the Ag 85A protein of Mycobacterium Tuberculosis afforded unprecedented levels of protective efficacy against aerosol challenge with virulent Mycobacterium bovis.
